title: Manjari 3. Meetings in Gauda and the Road to Vrindavana
html:
The bhava of Gadadhara Dasa; the darshana of Sita Thakurani and Jahnava; Srinivasa with Abhirama Gosani at Krishnanagara: the test of five gandas of cowries and the feeding of the Vaishnavas, three strokes of the whip "Jaya-mangala"; the road to Vrindavana

[p. 30]

Raga.

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3Thus some days passed in Navadvipa;
seeing and hearing, (Srinivasa) was amazed at heart.

4The bhava of a single devotee is deep as millions of oceans —
what wise man can fully measure it?

5Of Sri Gadadhara Dasa nothing can be understood:
outwardly nothing is seen, yet his heart always burns.

6Sometimes he sits and says nothing,
sometimes he moves here and there and laughs aloud.

7Speaking of Chaitanya, he brings up all sorts of stories;
at times he says and does things in great agitation.

8Now he speaks to himself in the subtlest voice,
as if in question and answer understanding everything fully.

[p. 31]

9Thrilled, full of tears, he laughs softly;
his body cannot be held for excess of joy.

10Biting his tongue with his teeth, he rolled his eyes,
sprang up as if in anger with a loud cry.

11He bites his lips, his brows quiver;
in anguish he speaks in faltering words.

12A moment later, again — as if mad:
rolling his reddened eyes, he looks in all directions.

13He sighs heavily, says nothing to anyone;
from inner pain his breast seems about to burst.

14And the next moment neither tears nor anything else is seen —
who can know the transformations of this bhava?

15One day someone, seeing his behaviour,
grew uneasy in his mind:

16"In separation from Chaitanya everyone's heart has melted,
yet this Thakura — why does he go about like this?"

17By chance one day he came close to him,
and Gadai's breath touched his body.

18That spot was scorched; he sprang up with a cry,
a moment later came to himself and fell down weeping.

19What had been in his mind
he told him all in private:

20"I offended you, not knowing you;
as was the offense, so the punishment I received."

[p. 32]

21Gosani says: "Go, do not fear;
may Gosani (the Lord) always be kind to all."

22When he is alone,
separation grows overwhelmingly strong in his heart.

23He falls senseless on the ground;
his whole body motionless, his breath does not move.

24Having lain thus for some time,
regaining consciousness, he suddenly sits up.

25How he laments then cannot be told;
at that time the whole mahabhava arises.

26Witnessing all these states of absorption in bhava,
(Srinivasa), amazed, reflected in his mind.

27What I heard from the lips of the mahantas,
this wondrous account, I have told very briefly.

28Meanwhile Sri Sita Thakurani,
mother of the world, the wife of Srila Advaita,

29Sri Jahnava, endowed with every shakti,
purifier of the fallen, the wife of Nityananda —

30the darshana of the feet of both he obtained in turn
and deemed his life fulfilled.

31Words would not come; tears, trembling, thrills;
he rises and falls again, not regaining awareness.

32The feet whose darshana grants fearlessness everywhere —
such darshana did Acharya Mahashaya obtain.

[p. 33]

33Thus he stayed there some days
and abundantly received the mercy of the feet of both.1

34Next — the meeting with Abhirama Gosani:
listen, all, attentively — it is most extraordinary.

35He heard from people about Krishnanagara:
Sri Abhirama Gosani lives there.2

36In Navadvipa, at the gate of the (Lord's) house, he bowed down
and placed on his head the dust of the feet of all the devotees.

37What transformations of bhava he had then —
who could describe them?

38In rapture he set out to see (Abhirama)
and gradually arrived there.

39He saw (Abhirama) seated with his associates,
his heart immersed in waves of talk about Krishna.

40At that moment (Srinivasa) came and offered dandavat obeisances;
he asks: "Who are you, what is your name?"

41Humbly he says: "My name is Srinivasa;
born in a brahmana family, I long for the Lord's darshana."

42Saying this, he took the dust of his feet;
(Abhirama), placing a hand on his head, was delighted.

43He said: "Stay here for some days;
whatever you need is all at your disposal."

44Telling the storekeeper to arrange everything,
he spoke of other things and then held talk about Krishna.

[p. 34]

45That day Thakura accepted sidha (uncooked provisions);
from the next day he lived, as usual, on his own.

46Bathing in the river, walks in the gardens on the bank,
beholding the service (of the Deity), hearing talk of Krishna.

47East of the house, while Rama-kunda was being dug,
Krishna appeared in person in the form of a Deity —

48named Sri Gopinatha, supremely enchanting;
(Abhirama) serves Him in countless special ways.3

49There (Srinivasa) found the limit of happiness and stayed;
all the money he had ran out.

50After that, the vessels he had with him
were also sold off little by little.

51When at the end five gandas of cowries remained,
that day Gosani gave a certain order:

52"Hey, my boy, today in a rich man's house
there will be a wedding — go there quickly.

53Today's meal you will get first,
and on the dakshina you will live five more days."

54Hearing this, Thakura kept silent;
Gosani began to say the same again.

55Then Thakura said: "I have enough to live on."
"What do you have? Tell the truth," Gosani asks.

56When he heard, "I have five gandas of cowries,"
astonished, he thought to himself:

[p. 35]

57"Today I shall test him: let me see what the brahmana does."
To people he says: "See where he cooks."

58Thakura bought rice for sixteen cowries,
took a clay pot for one cowrie,

59firewood for two cowries, salt for one,
and with these went to the river Darukeshvara.

60In the garden there are many banana leaves:
they are had for nothing, no one buys them.

61When, having bathed there, he set the rice to cook,
a spy came and told Gosani everything.

62Gosani said: "Go, four Vaishnavas,
to where Srinivasa is cooking.

63Stay hidden, do not show yourselves at first;
only when he has offered the bhoga, go near."

64Receiving Gosani's order, they went
and appeared just as he finished the offering.

65Distinctly chanting the names "Hare Krishna",
they all came up before Thakura.

66In the garb of renunciants — waist-string, water pot, kaupina,
patched quilt — the marks of great detachment were seen.

67Seeing them, he was very glad
and humbly began to speak:

68"If out of mercy you have come — it is my good fortune;
please accept some of this prasada rice."

[p. 36]

69They say: "We shall do as you have said."
Thakura says: "Then you have bought me."

70On one side he seated the four Vaishnavas
and prepared five banana-leaf tips.

71Serving the (rice) there in equal portions,
he put a pinch of salt for each.

72Having seated them, he sat down himself;
having eaten, they were very pleased.

73Satisfied, they took leave and went
and, coming to Gosani, told him everything.

74As soon as he heard it, he was overcome with prema
and began to speak in a faltering voice:

75"In Chaitanya's time I saw such renunciation —
and it exists even today! At this I marvel.

76I used to say: 'That Thief has carried everything off' —
and for that my heart always burns.

77Now I know: here and there, a little,
He has left it behind — this has become evident."

78As he said this, the former happiness came back to him:
surging up, with a loud cry he fell to the ground.

79His breath does not move, not a limb stirs;
seeing this, all the Vaishnavas cry out in alarm.

80For some time he lies senseless in bliss;
then Acharya Thakura comes up.

[p. 37]

81He heard all that had happened, saw his state,
and streams (of tears) began to flow down his face and breast.

82Hear further of the transformations of his prema:
after Mahaprabhu's disappearance he showed the signs of (prema's) madness.

83Nowhere seeing that gift of prema,
seeing joylessness everywhere, he constantly suffers.

84There is a horsewhip named "Jaya-mangala":
striking people with it, he makes them overwhelmed with prema.4

85When in the third prahara he regained consciousness,
the eight sattvika bhavas appeared in his body.

86Thus after some time, half returned to outer awareness,
he sees Srinivasa standing before him.

87Having the whip brought from a servant's hand,
he strikes Thakura as if with an angry face.

88When he had struck him three times with that whip,
Malini, in alarm, seized his hand:5

89"You have flooded him! What more do you want to do?
Look just once at the state that has come upon him!"

90One sees thrills, tears, trembling — he shakes all over;
pallor, a breaking voice, he cannot utter a sound.

91Now sweat breaks out, now he stands stiff as a post,
now he is restless like a madman.

92Whatever sanchari bhava comes into his mind,
so he acts at that moment — it cannot be told.

[p. 38]

93Again Malini says: "Gosani, what have you done!
You have spoiled the brahmana youth's studies.

94Show mercy, so that the signs of madness
do not hinder his study of the scriptures of truth."

95Thakura humbly fell down in obeisance;
Gosani placed his foot on his head,

96took him on his lap and, holding his chin,
spoke sweet words, absorbed in prema:

97"Do not worry about anything — what the Creator has ordained (will be);
go to Vrindavana — there all perfection will come."

98Saying this, embracing, they began to weep;
both were in turmoil at the coming separation.

99So the dust of the feet of all the devotees
he took again and again and placed on his head.

100That night he passed absorbed in bhava;
rising, he sees a little of the night remains.

101Then he went out beyond the gate of the house
and, unable to compose himself, offered dandavat obeisances.

102For a long time he wept there, rolling on the ground;
regaining awareness, he turned his face toward Vrindavana.

103All day he walks as far as he can;
wherever evening falls, there he halts.

104If he receives something unasked, he cooks
and eats; if he receives nothing, he fasts.

[p. 39]

105Body and mind always overflowing with the divine madness of bhava,
he walks without fear; hunger and thirst do not hinder him.

106When stupor or swoon comes upon him,
he lies fallen, and people think he is tired from the road.

107After some days he came to Sri Mathura;
as soon as he saw its beauty, he was absorbed in bhava.

108Collecting himself, he came to the Vishranti tirtha;
bathing and drinking water, he was rid of his bodily fatigue.

109There the people of Mathura were talking among themselves —
and there he heard of Sri Rupa's disappearance.

110Hastily approaching one of them, he asked for news,
and he told of the departure of the three Gosanis:

111"Sanatana withdrew (from the manifest world) many days ago;
after him, by his own will, Raghunatha Bhatta.

112Recently, some days ago, Rupa disappeared.
So I have told you about these three."

113As soon as he heard this, he turned pale;
he wants to lament, but no sound leaves his throat.

114His body thrills, streams of tears flow from his eyes;
sweat gleams on his face like scattered pearls.

115A trembling runs over his body, seizing it entirely;
a moment later, helpless, his throat rattles.

116He fell senseless to the ground, unconscious;
his body became motionless and remained so for some time.

[p. 40]

117Regaining consciousness, he rolls on the ground again,
like a golden image tossing in the dust.

118With cries he laments in such a way
that, hearing it, no one could keep his composure.

119All around, weeping, people ask what has happened;
who will answer? — there is no consolation at all.

120As soon as he heard the news of the Gosanis,
he was distraught — the wise know this.

121At that time no one travelled to and from
Vrindavana: the road was very dangerous.

122For fear of robbers and beasts no one can pass along the road;
if anyone carries money tied on him, he is killed at once.

123Only one with such longing can come;
the Lord's will is beyond the reach of reasoning.

124So no news (from Vrindavana) can be had;
one learns everything only on reaching Mathura.

125Such was formerly the road to Vrindavana;
some time later travelling to and fro became safe.

126In a moment a bhava arose with the signs of madness;
in the midst of it he made this resolve:

127"I came to Vrindavana with a firm intention:
as soon as I arrived, I would take shelter at Rupa's feet,

128study the Sri Bhagavata with Raghunatha,
and serve Sanatana with body, mind and word.

[p. 41]

129If that has not come about — why go on?
Death does not come, nor does a thunderbolt fall on my head!"

130As he thought thus, a tempest of anxiety arose;
his judgement was lost, he grew utterly restless.

131He turned back, heeding neither what lay ahead nor behind,
and walked as far as he could until evening.

132Hungry, thirsty, stricken with grief, exhausted,
his body gave way; he fell and lay there.

133Distraught with thoughts, at night not a wink of sleep;
only at the end of the night a light doze came.

134In that place he received the darshana of Sri Rupa;
gazing at him, he knew that the name "Rupa" (beauty) was true.6

135Not very tall, full-bodied, a shapely form,
a golden complexion outshining the flash of lightning.

136Shaven, in the garb of renunciation, only the shikha flutters in the wind;
a high nose, on his lips the glow of dawn.

137Beautifully red palms and soles shine,
and on them the light of the moons of the nails.

138A body fashioned as if from love, most tender;
his speech — what streams of nectar!

139On his forehead a tilaka shaped like the temple of Hari;
the ornament of his neck a necklace of tulasi.

140Seeing him thus, he fell down in dandavat obeisance;
unable to contain his bliss, tears flow down his breast.

[p. 42]

141When he had bowed down once, twice, three, four times,
then (Rupa) placed his foot on his head,

142raised him, took him on his lap, and with sweetest words
began to speak — hearing them, life is soothed:

143"By my order, go back to Vrindavana;
study the books of bhakti with Jiva.

144By my mercy their meaning will be fully revealed to you;
in a few days, having studied the scriptures, you will become a teacher.

145You wished to be initiated by me for worship;
but that (I) — and Gopala Bhatta: there is no difference.

146Go to him and be initiated by him;
every perfection will come — accept this word of mine."

147Saying this, casting a merciful glance with tears,
he vanished; and here (Srinivasa) sprang up with a cry.

148"Ha Rupa! Ha Rupa!" — he rolls on the ground;
hearing that lament, life leaves the body.

149At the sound of weeping people ran up and surrounded him
and began with all care to ask:

150"Who are you, and why are you so distraught?
Hearing of your grief, the heart breaks."

151Thakura, ceaselessly intoxicated with the absorption of bhava,
hears nothing — whoever speaks and however much.

152Seeing his anguish, the people were distressed;
tears flow down everyone's breast.

[p. 43]

153As he lamented thus for some time,
his body grew limp — suddenly he swooned.

154He lay there, not a limb stirring;
seeing this, the people cry out in grief.

155For a moment he remained thus, stunned;
then he sat up again, regaining consciousness.

156He reflected: "The order that Gosani has given —
that is my goal; in it I see my welfare."

157Rising, he set off on the road to Vrindavana;
he sees nothing — his eyes are full of tears.

158When Sri Acharya Thakura set out
for Sri Vrindavana, his heart overflowing with the rapture of prema —

159here, in that same part of the night, to Jiva Gosani
Sri Rupa speaks lovingly in a dream:

160"On the Vaishakha full moon, at the time of the evening arati,
a brahmana who comes from the land of Gauda

161will behold Sri Govinda from behind everyone,
absorbed in prema — so it is ordained.

162His body is golden, his name is Srinivasa;
by my order, place your trust in him."

163In separation Gopala Bhatta Gosani day and night,
waking and sleeping, converses in visions with Sri Rupa.

164That night (Rupa) told him: "The brahmana youth
who will come today — accept him."

[p. 44]

165Thus before evening he arrived in Vrindavana;
seeing the temple enclosure, he asked what was happening there.7

166People say: "It is the time of Govinda's arati;
go quickly for darshana, if you wish."

167As soon as he heard it, he ran in haste;
but in the great crowd he could not get in.

168Standing behind, he gazed at the (Lord's) lotus face,
but his eyes filled with tears — he sees nothing.

169When the arati was over, the crowd still being great,
Thakura went and sat to one side.

170Tears, trembling, thrills are seen on his body;
the joy of beholding the face cannot be contained in it.

171Meanwhile Sri Jiva Gosani looked everywhere,
but in the great crowd could not see him anywhere.

172Greatly surprised, he reflects in his mind:
"Gosani told me this for certain.

173Can his word ever turn out otherwise?
The crowd has gone — what can be done now?"

174Reflecting thus, taking five or seven people,
he himself goes about searching everywhere.

175He sees that near the door, inside, there is a place:
"It seems to me someone is sitting there."

[p. 45]

176Going there himself,
seeing the absorption of bhava, he was delighted.

177He saw that it all agreed with Sri Gosani-jiu's order
and, to remove all doubt, began to question him.

178Thakura, looking, knew him to be Sri Jiva Gosani,
hastily wiped his tears and fell (at his feet) right there.

179Whoever hears of his humility at that time —
let alone men, even stone would melt.

180Raising him respectfully, Gosani embraced him
and, in tears, speaks in faltering words:

181"Sri Gosani told me about you;
it is good that I have seen you so soon.

182By my good fortune my Prabhu has been kind
and joined me with such a friend as you.

183We shall live together, no one will go anywhere,
we shall ceaselessly relish talk of Krishna."

184Thakura told everything about the dream;
hearing it, he embraced him again and again in bliss.

185Taking him by the hand, he brought him to Govinda's cook
and through the cook had him partake of prasada,

186brought him to his own lodging and gave him a place to stay,
where he was provided for in every way.

187Thus passing that night there,
early in the morning, having bathed in the Yamuna and so on,

188Gosani himself, taking Thakura with him,
came to Sri Radha-ramana, rejoicing.

[p. 46]

189They saw Gopala Bhatta seated;
step by step they went up to that place.

190Greeting him fittingly, they sat down on seats
and told all the news from beginning to end.

191As soon as he heard it, Bhatta Gosani was overwhelmed;
he says: "Yesterday I received such a command (in a dream)."

192In separation from Sri Rupa the Bhatta grieved boundlessly:
"What shall I do with a disciple? The body has become a burden to me."

193And yet, hearing of the dreams of both
and thinking of his own dream, he showed him great honour:

194"His order is my duty;
whatever he says at any time I shall do gladly.

195I know: Sri Gosani, being gracious to me,
has joined me with a priceless jewel."

196Hearing these words, Sri Acharya Thakura
fell down in dandavat obeisance and remained, bathed in tears.

197Then Sri Jiva Gosani speaks:
"Tomorrow, on the second lunar day — I think it good."

198"So be it: whatever has come from your lips
has no flaw in it — it is excellent in every way."

199Saying this, Bhatta Gosani, with anguish on his face,
compassionately asks for news of the land of Gauda.

200Hearing of the state of Mahaprabhu's family,
all three wept long, sobbing aloud.

[p. 47]

201Who can describe the weeping at that time?
Not to speak of people — trees and stones were rent.

202Thus for some time they talked of the Beloved (Lord);
then (Srinivasa) asked leave to go to his lodging.

203Gosani had dry prasada brought and gave it to him,
and, giving him darshana of Thakura (the Deity), sent him off.

204Both bowed down, Bhatta Gosani embraced (them);
thus that day he went to his lodging.

205Early in the morning, having bathed and so on in the same way,
he came quickly together with Sri Jiva Gosani.

206Bhatta Gosani was engaged in the service of Thakura (the Deity);
offering obeisances and praises, both sat down on seats.

207The articles of worship that Sri Jiva Gosvami had prepared
he placed in Acharya Thakura's hands and led him (there).

208Accepting them, Bhatta Gosani performed the service;
compassion filled his body beyond restraint.

209First he bestowed the mercy of the name of Sri Hari,
then the two incomparable mantras of Radha and Krishna.

210Having made him hear the five names, he gave him a siddha name:
"Sri Mani-manjari" — (Srinivasa) heard from the guru's lips.8

211His own name he gives as Sri Guna-manjari,
holding to what Sri Rupa wrote in the Ganoddesha.9

[p. 48]

212Thus (the shloka): "Lavanga-manjari, Rupa-manjari, Guna-manjari, Bhanumati — another name of the first — the very dear Rati-manjari, Ragalekha, Kalakeli, Manjula and others are maidservants."

213Friends devoted to service, foremost in attendance —
therefore the account calls them maidservants.

214This parakiya-lila in Vraja, in Vrindavana —
Sri Rupa showed the way to it in the Smarana-mangala.10

215All follow within the group of Sri Rupa-manjari;
as is one's meditation, so is one's attainment.

216Sri Radha-ramana is the son of the king of Vraja;
Radha has no contact with Vasudeva and the others.

217Therefore Sri Rupa Gosani's desire
he expressed so that we may know the path of worship.

218Thus (the verse) of Srimad Rupa: "Your parents are the lord and lady of the cowherds; O Holder of the mountain, Sri Radhika is Your beloved; Sridama, Subala and others are Your friends; Nilambara is Your elder brother; the flute is Your instrument, the peacock feather Your ornament, Nandishvara Your home, the forest of Vrindavana Your pleasure garden; beyond this, O Lord, I know no other form of Yours."11

219That Radha-ramana is the son of Shachi;
always meditate on Them as non-different.

220A verse of the Bhagavata, as a definition,
Sri Rupa expounded in the Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-ashtaka.

[p. 49]

221Thus in the Sri Bhagavata: "Thus, O king, in Dvapara they praise the Lord of the universe; hear now how in Kali (He is worshipped) according to the injunctions of various tantras: in Kali intelligent people worship, with sacrifices consisting chiefly of sankirtana, Him who chants (the name of) Krishna, whose complexion is not dark, together with His parts, intimates, weapons and associates."12

222Shlokas from Sri Rupa's hymn: "He whom the wise in Kali openly worship with sacrifices consisting of loud kirtana — Krishna, whose body is not dark owing to the abundance of His radiance; whom they call the object of worship of all who have entered the fourth ashrama — may that God in the form of Chaitanya be exceedingly merciful to us! — He who, eager to steal and taste the sweet, unfathomable fullness of rasa of one among His loving ones, covered His own colour, manifesting here her radiance — may that God in the form of Chaitanya be exceedingly merciful to us!"13

223Spoken by Srimad Dasa Gosvami: "Perform neither the dharma nor the adharma described in the shrutis; here in Vraja render abundant service to Radha and Krishna; O mind, always remember the son of Shachi as the son of the lord of Nandishvara, and the best guru as dear to Mukunda."14

224The settled sense and intent of these three shlokas:
Sri Shachinandana is the son of the king of Vraja.

225Accepting the bhava and radiance of Sri Radhika,
Gaurahari descended in Sri Navadvipa.

[p. 50]

226The son of the king of Vraja tried hard in Vraja,
(but) three desires of His heart were not fulfilled:

227"What is the nature of Radha's prema for Me —
this I cannot grasp, however I try.

228How is My sweetness tasted,
and what is Radhika's bliss?

229The ocean of bliss Sri Radhika has from My touch —
not one drop of it can I taste.

230Therefore, without accepting Radha's bhava,
these three tastes cannot be achieved."

231The source of avataras descended — that is the root purpose;
the incidental one is the establishment of the yuga-dharma.

232When the source of avataras becomes manifest,
the separate yuga-avatara does not remain apart:

233the avatara enters into the source of avataras.
The condensed essence of the meaning I have now set forth.15

234Then Gosvami-jiu had an apprehension —
the interpretation of those averse (to the Lord) came to his mind:

235if they say: Mahaprabhu took sannyasa,
and by accepting the danda He is a manifestation of Narayana,

236and that it is with this in view that (Sri Rupa) speaks of such glory,
and think, "This is the intent, I have reached the limit" —

237no, it is not so: the assembly of sannyasis of the fourth ashrama —
their object of worship is He, the son of the king of Vraja.16

[p. 51]

238He imparted to (Srinivasa) the most secret essence,
knowing him in every way a vessel of Sri Rupa's mercy.

239"So much about worship have I told you;
gradually knowledge of its details will come.

240In the Hari-bhakti-vilasa and the Rasamrita-sindhu
the order of service and sadhana is clearly set out.

241But — according to the practitioner's qualification;
you will see the whole arrangement for yourself."

242Thakura, sitting in solitude, recited the mantras in order within
and everywhere, as was fitting, offered dandavat obeisances.

243Then, having performed the midday arati,
distributing chatuhsama, tulasi buds and so on,

244they brought wonderful prasada cooked in ghee
and served it in various kinds.

245Until Bhatta Gosani sits, neither of the two will sit;
knowing this, he sat down, and someone else served.

246All who there bore the name of Vaishnava
were brought and seated first.

247Relishing all kinds of talk about Krishna,
in bliss they partook of maha-prasada.

248After rinsing hands and mouth, camphor betel was given,
sandal paste on the whole body and a prasada garland on the neck.

249Satisfied, all went to their own lodgings.
Thus (Srinivasa) settled in Vrindavana.

[p. 52]

250Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

251Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, in the life of Srimad Acharya Thakura, the third manjari, called "The Mercy of Sri Gopala Bhatta".

Notes

  1. According to the Prema-vilasa (4–5), Srinivasa sees Sita at Shantipura and Jahnava at Khardaha; here no places are named.
  2. Krishnanagara — Abhirama's (Ramadasa's) village on the Darukeshvara, near Khanakul.
  3. According to the author, Abhirama's Deity of Gopinatha appeared when Rama-kunda was being dug; the Deity is Krishna Himself, appearing in the form of a Deity.
  4. Abhirama's whip "Jaya-mangala": whoever he struck with it was filled with prema (cf. Prema-vilasa 5).
  5. Malini is apparently Abhirama's wife (as in the Prema-vilasa 5). In the Prema-vilasa Srinivasa comes to Abhirama with Vishnupriya's letter and with Ishana, Abhirama gives him eight karas of cowries, and two Vaishnavas are sent to him; in Manohara Dasa it is five gandas of cowries and four Vaishnavas, while Srinivasa comes on his own and stays a long time.
  6. According to the Prema-vilasa (6), Rupa and Sanatana appear to Srinivasa in a dream under a tree when in despair he wants to turn back; in Manohara Dasa it is Rupa alone, and he directly sends Srinivasa to Gopala Bhatta for initiation.
  7. "Chakra-ber" — the enclosure of the temple courtyard (cf. 4.14).
  8. Srinivasa's siddha name is Mani-manjari, as in the Prema-vilasa (6, 19). The "five names" are apparently the fivefold instruction given at initiation; the exact sense is unclear.
  9. I.e. according to Sri Rupa's Radha-Krishna-ganoddesha-dipika, where Guna-manjari is named among Radha's maidservants.
  10. The Smarana-mangala — Sri Rupa's eleven verses on the eightfold daily pastimes of Radha and Krishna. Parakiya — the love of the gopis outside the bond of marriage; according to Srila Bhaktisiddhanta's teaching it is the highest transcendental love, having nothing in common with a worldly liaison.
  11. A verse from Sri Rupa's Stava-mala.
  12. Bhagavata 11.5.31–32.
  13. From Sri Rupa's first Chaitanya-ashtaka (Stava-mala).
  14. Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami's Manah-shiksha, 2.
  15. Cf. CC Adi 4 (Krishna's three desires) and Adi 3–4 (the yuga-avatara enters into Svayam Bhagavan).
  16. I.e. Mahaprabhu is worshipped not as a sannyasi (in the Mayavadi view a sannyasi who takes the danda is "Narayana") but as Krishna Himself, whom even sannyasis worship.
